# Small intestinal fungal overgrowth

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Gastroenterology > Diseases of the intestine and appendix > Small intestinal fungal overgrowth*

[Original Article Link](/library/ww0hOR)

---

## Summary

Small intestinal fungal overgrowth (SIFO) is a form of dysbiosis caused by the excessive growth of fungi (primarily <u>Candida</u> species) in the <u>small intestine</u>. The existence and clinical relevance of SIFO as a distinct entity remain debated. <u>Risk factors</u> include <u>immunosuppression</u> caused by conditions like <u>HIV</u> or cancer, the use of medications (e.g., <u>corticosteroids</u> or <u>proton pump inhibitors</u>), and impaired <u>gut motility</u>. Clinical features are nonspecific and are similar to those of <u>small intestinal bacterial overgrowth</u> (<u>SIBO</u>), including abdominal <u>pain</u>, <u>bloating</u>, gas, and <u>diarrhea</u>. The diagnosis of SIFO is challenging. Invasive fungal culture of a small intestinal <u>aspirate</u> can confirm the diagnosis, especially in patients with typical symptoms that do not improve after <u>antibiotic</u> treatment. Management is tailored to the individual patient and primarily involves <u>antifungal agents</u>, e.g., <u>fluconazole</u>. Dietary approaches, probiotics, and lifestyle modifications can also be part of the treatment plan. Potential complications of SIFO include <u>malabsorption</u> and <u>malnutrition</u>.
